hero.title: US–Iran Diplomacy, Energy Prices and Trump–Xi Talks Dominate Global Agenda
hero.description: Diplomatic efforts continue alongside the US–Iran conflict as the UN General Assembly enters a critical phase. Ukraine is pressing for an energy truce, European governments are responding to high fuel costs, Nigeria faces renewed petrol-price pressure, and the Trump–Xi summit puts trade and technology back in focus.

featured.title: US–Iran Diplomacy Remains Open as Energy Markets Watch Hormuz
featured.content: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the UN General Assembly that Iran would not surrender to US pressure while maintaining that diplomacy remains possible. Washington and Tehran remain far apart on how to end the conflict. The Strait of Hormuz remains a major concern for global energy markets, with Iran having indicated that it could reopen the waterway if US military pressure and the blockade are eased. Any sustained disruption would have implications for oil, shipping, transport and consumer prices worldwide. 8

articles.title: US–Iran: Diplomacy Continues While Conflict Remains Unresolved
articles.content: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian used his UN address to say Iran would not surrender to US pressure, while also maintaining that diplomacy can provide a route towards ending the conflict. Reuters reports that US and Iranian positions remain far apart. The Strait of Hormuz is central to the discussions because disruption of the waterway can affect global energy and shipping supplies. 9
articles.imageQuery: Iran United States diplomacy UN General Assembly

articles.title: Hormuz Remains Critical to Global Energy Security
articles.content: A senior Iranian official has said Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure and lifts its blockade. The statement is part of wider diplomatic discussions and does not represent a confirmed reopening agreement. 10
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz tanker oil shipping

articles.title: Ukraine Pushes for Energy Truce Before Winter
articles.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is seeking an agreement to halt attacks on energy infrastructure. He has warned that Ukraine could retaliate against Russian energy targets if an arrangement cannot be reached. Reuters reports that Ukraine is ready to discuss different formats for an energy ceasefire, but there is no confirmed comprehensive energy truce at this stage. 11
articles.imageQuery: Volodymyr Zelenskyy United Nations New York

articles.title: Europe Responds to Rising Energy and Fuel Costs
articles.content: Higher global energy prices are putting pressure on European households, transport operators and businesses. France has expanded targeted fuel-price relief, while Germany has announced a temporary €0.17-per-litre reduction in petrol and diesel taxes from October 1 through the end of 2026. European governments are also examining wider measures to cushion the economic impact. 12
articles.imageQuery: European petrol station fuel prices energy crisis

articles.title: Nigeria: Rising Petrol Prices Put Cost of Living Back in Focus
articles.content: Nigeria is experiencing renewed fuel-price pressure as international crude prices rise. Reuters reports petrol prices of around ₦1,400 per litre in Lagos and Abuja and up to approximately ₦1,500 in some northern locations, while diesel has exceeded ₦2,000 per litre in some markets. The developments show how international crude prices continue to affect Nigeria despite the Dangote Refinery operating at high capacity. 13
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria petrol filling station fuel prices

articles.title: Dangote Refinery IPO Attracts Strong Retail Interest
articles.content: The Dangote Refinery IPO continues to attract substantial attention from Nigerian retail investors. Reuters previously reported that strong demand caused several digital investment platforms to experience outages. The IPO is therefore also testing the capacity of Nigeria's growing digital investment infrastructure. Investors should remember that buying shares carries risk and strong demand does not guarantee future returns. 14

articles.title: Global Oil Markets Remain Highly Sensitive to Middle East Developments
articles.content: Oil markets remain volatile as traders assess the US–Iran conflict, possible diplomatic developments and the future of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Recent Reuters reporting shows Brent crude has remained above $100 a barrel during periods of heightened supply concern. 15

articles.title: Trump–Xi Talks Put AI, Trade and Technology in Focus
articles.content: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are meeting in Washington during Xi's September 23–25 visit. Trade, technology, artificial intelligence, Taiwan and the wider US–China relationship are among the major issues surrounding the summit. The two governments are seeking to manage competition while maintaining high-level communication. 16
articles.imageQuery: Donald Trump Xi Jinping Washington meeting

articles.title: AI Security Becomes a Bigger International Issue
articles.content: Artificial intelligence remains a major part of US–China technology competition, particularly around advanced chips, AI supply chains and security. The issue is also increasingly being discussed through international institutions as governments consider how to manage the opportunities and risks associated with rapidly developing AI systems. 17

articles.title: Japan Factory Growth Slows in September
articles.content: Japan's manufacturing activity continued to expand in September, but growth slowed compared with August as output and new orders softened. The latest PMI reading points to continued industrial activity while highlighting changing demand and cost conditions for Japanese manufacturers. 18

articles.title: Europe Faces Continued Jet Fuel and Diesel Supply Pressure
articles.content: Europe is facing continued pressure in refined-fuel markets. Reuters reports that Europe is expected to face a fourth-quarter jet-fuel supply deficit while global diesel prices have reached record levels amid disruptions linked to the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine. 19
